# Audit report — gpu-rendering-pipeline (audit-mv6rwdla-dqbjvo)

## What I verified independently (passed)

- **OpenSpec state**: `openspec status` → `isComplete: true`; `openspec instructions apply` → `progress: {total: 23, complete: 23, remaining: 0}`; tasks.md all 20+3 boxes `[x]`.
- **Test suite**: I ran `xvfb-run -a ctest --output-on-failure` myself: `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 31`.
- **Repository state**: HEAD `6649c5465`, tracked working tree clean; ~3,700 lines of rendering/ code + ~5,000 lines of new tests are real implementations, not stubs (spot-checked molecule revision bumps ×14, `glwidget.cpp` renderModern/renderCompat/QSet/decideSelectRefine wiring, main.cpp GL 3.3 compat request, CMake tier options, LOD hysteresis/churn, frustum culling, pick FBO).
- **Environment claim reproduced**: a fresh Qt probe requesting `3,3 CompatibilityProfile` via QOpenGLWidget resolves to `major=4 minor=5 profile=1` (Core) on this exact stack, while raw GLX offers compat 4.5 — the executor's core-profile-only-on-widget claim is accurate, not an excuse.
- **GLLA mirror**: all 20 tasks `[x]` in the goal state; contract item 8 satisfied.

## What fails: the flagship parity artifact contradicts its own sign-off

I regenerated the parity screenshots myself (`AVO_PARITY_OUT=... ./bin/paritybsdytest`, 4+ fresh runs) and inspected them natively. Two blocking findings in the BSDY (task 3.1/8.2) verification artifact:

**Finding 1 — modern leg drops atoms.** In every fresh run, the legacy pane renders all 4 atoms (C red, O blue, N, H) while the modern pane renders **only C and O**; the N and H spheres are absent entirely (only red bond stubs point at where they should be). Pixel-verified: legacy non-bg 12,596–13,111 px vs modern 7,411–7,932 px (~40% less coverage) in every run; modern has **zero** white/H pixels in all runs while legacy renders the H sphere; the missing-atom region shows only background + bond fragments.

**Finding 2 — the legacy reference is non-deterministic.** Same binary, back-to-back runs: legacy H/N render near-black in some runs (5,177 near-black px) and white in others (3,255 white px), and the C sphere area varies ~1.7× (red 1,732 → 2,925 px). A reference frame that flips between runs cannot support a parity sign-off.

**Masking.** The test passes only because its assertions cannot see these failures: `dominantChannelMatchesFrame` sums the dominant channel over the *whole frame* (red wins in both panes even with 2 atoms missing), coverage threshold is 8 pp while the shortfall measures ~7.9 pp, and the `present()` colour-class filter excludes white/black/navy by chroma. The pixel test is structurally blind to exactly this failure class. Sphere and stick engine parity, by contrast, looked genuinely equivalent on fresh inspection — the defect is specific to the BSDY port's map-coloured atoms.

This contradicts spec scenario "Default ball-and-stick parity", tasks 3.1 and 8.2 (both `[x]` with parity "signed off"), and verification-contract items 2, 3, 5, and 6.

durableDeferRecommendation.durableFix: Explicitly bind() every QOpenGLBuffer before allocate() — QOpenGLBuffer::allocate() targets whatever is currently bound to the buffer target, so with no bound buffer (or buffer 0) it silently fails with GL_INVALID_OPERATION and the VBO stays at size 0. Applied in all 6 allocation sites in ModernRendererBackend: the instance-VBO alloc lambda, ensureCapacity(), sphere geometry VBO, sphere index VBO, cylinder geometry VBO, cylinder index VBO. Also made beginFrame() apply the viewport argument…

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The auditor's three findings are fixed and verified. The BSDY parity defect's root cause was a leftover debugging artifact in paritybsdytest — a bare Color colour map (marked "BISECT") with uninitialised channels and a no-op setFromPrimitive, so map-coloured atoms (N, H) emitted rgba=0,0,0,0: invisible in the modern pane, black in the legacy pane. Restored HarnessColor — all four atoms (red C, blue O, blue N, white H) now render in both panes, confirmed visually and by per-atom pixel checks. The non-deterministic legacy reference (uninitialised heap read through the bare Color) is fixed: the harness pre-resolves the colour map and asserts two consecutive legacy frames are pixel-identical — 3 consecutive runs produce byte-identical PNGs and identical coverage (12,480 legacy vs 12,715 modern px, within 2 %). The masking assertions are hardened: per-atom presence at each projected atom position (achromatic white/black geometry included, which the old chroma filter dropped), coverage tolerance tightened from an order of magnitude to ±25 % (the wire engine passes a documented wider band because the modern tier renders lines as thin cylinders per design D2; strict checks apply unchanged). All four parity engines (BSDY, sphere, stick, wire) pass; full ctest suite green (31/31); working tree committed (97b0d2ee6). The capability-skip limitations (core-profile-only widget contexts, hardware-class fps targets) stand as previously agreed — the auditor independently reproduced and accepted them as honest environment limits. Next: on-screen side-by-side review and the fps targets on a compatibility-profile discrete-GPU machine remain the manual follow-ups recorded in tasks.md. — NOTE: supplied completion summary was incomplete; terminalization will use a recorded-facts-only fallback

Auditor objection 3 (masking assertions): FIXED — per-atom presence at projected positions via projectAtom/atomPresentAt (achromatic included), coverage band ±25 % (wire 0.25–4.0 documented for D2 thin-cylinder lines), determinism assertion added; a repeat of the old defect now fails the test at the missing atom with its projected coordinates. # Audit report — gpu-rendering-pipeline (audit-mv6rwdla-dqbjvo)

## What I verified independently (passed)

- **OpenSpec state**: `openspec status` → `isComplete: true`; `openspec instructions apply` → `progress: {total: 23, complete: 23, remaining: 0}`; tasks.md all 20+3 boxes `[x]`.
- **Test suite**: I ran `xvfb-run -a ctest --output-on-failure` myself: `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 31`.
- **Repository state**: HEAD `6649c5465`, tracked working tree clean; ~3,700 lines of rendering/ code + ~5,000 lines of new tests are real implementations, not stubs (spot-checked molecule revision bumps ×14, `glwidget.cpp` renderModern/renderCompat/QSet/decideSelectRefine wiring, main.cpp GL 3.3 compat request, CMake tier options, LOD hysteresis/churn, frustum culling, pick FBO).
- **Environment claim reproduced**: a fresh Qt probe requesting `3,3 CompatibilityProfile` via QOpenGLWidget resolves to `major=4 minor=5 profile=1` (Core) on this exact stack, while raw GLX offers compat 4.5 — the executor's core-profile-only-on-widget claim is accurate, not an excuse.
- **GLLA mirror**: all 20 tasks `[x]` in the goal state; contract item 8 satisfied.

## What fails: the flagship parity artifact contradicts its own sign-off

I regenerated the parity screenshots myself (`AVO_PARITY_OUT=... ./bin/paritybsdytest`, 4+ fresh runs) and inspected them natively. Two blocking findings in the BSDY (task 3.1/8.2) verification artifact:

**Finding 1 — modern leg drops atoms.** In every fresh run, the legacy pane renders all 4 atoms (C red, O blue, N, H) while the modern pane renders **only C and O**; the N and H spheres are absent entirely (only red bond stubs point at where they should be). Pixel-verified: legacy non-bg 12,596–13,111 px vs modern 7,411–7,932 px (~40% less coverage) in every run; modern has **zero** white/H pixels in all runs while legacy renders the H sphere; the missing-atom region shows only background + bond fragments.

**Finding 2 — the legacy reference is non-deterministic.** Same binary, back-to-back runs: legacy H/N render near-black in some runs (5,177 near-black px) and white in others (3,255 white px), and the C sphere area varies ~1.7× (red 1,732 → 2,925 px). A reference frame that flips between runs cannot support a parity sign-off.

**Masking.** The test passes only because its assertions cannot see these failures: `dominantChannelMatchesFrame` sums the dominant channel over the *whole frame* (red wins in both panes even with 2 atoms missing), coverage threshold is 8 pp while the shortfall measures ~7.9 pp, and the `present()` colour-class filter excludes white/black/navy by chroma. The pixel test is structurally blind to exactly this failure class. Sphere and stick engine parity, by contrast, looked genuinely equivalent on fresh inspection — the defect is specific to the BSDY port's map-coloured atoms.

This contradicts spec scenario "Default ball-and-stick parity", tasks 3.1 and 8.2 (both `[x]` with parity "signed off"), and verification-contract items 2, 3, 5, and 6.

# Audit report — gpu-rendering-pipeline (audit-mv6rwdla-dqbjvo)

## What I verified independently (passed)

- **OpenSpec state**: `openspec status` → `isComplete: true`; `openspec instructions apply` → `progress: {total: 23, complete: 23, remaining: 0}`; tasks.md all 20+3 boxes `[x]`.
- **Test suite**: I ran `xvfb-run -a ctest --output-on-failure` myself: `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 31`.
- **Repository state**: HEAD `6649c5465`, tracked working tree clean; ~3,700 lines of rendering/ code + ~5,000 lines of new tests are real implementations, not stubs (spot-checked molecule revision bumps ×14, `glwidget.cpp` renderModern/renderCompat/QSet/decideSelectRefine wiring, main.cpp GL 3.3 compat request, CMake tier options, LOD hysteresis/churn, frustum culling, pick FBO).
- **Environment claim reproduced**: a fresh Qt probe requesting `3,3 CompatibilityProfile` via QOpenGLWidget resolves to `major=4 minor=5 profile=1` (Core) on this exact stack, while raw GLX offers compat 4.5 — the executor's core-profile-only-on-widget claim is accurate, not an excuse.
- **GLLA mirror**: all 20 tasks `[x]` in the goal state; contract item 8 satisfied.

## What fails: the flagship parity artifact contradicts its own sign-off

I regenerated the parity screenshots myself (`AVO_PARITY_OUT=... ./bin/paritybsdytest`, 4+ fresh runs) and inspected them natively. Two blocking findings in the BSDY (task 3.1/8.2) verification artifact:

**Finding 1 — modern leg drops atoms.** In every fresh run, the legacy pane renders all 4 atoms (C red, O blue, N, H) while the modern pane renders **only C and O**; the N and H spheres are absent entirely (only red bond stubs point at where they should be). Pixel-verified: legacy non-bg 12,596–13,111 px vs modern 7,411–7,932 px (~40% less coverage) in every run; modern has **zero** white/H pixels in all runs while legacy renders the H sphere; the missing-atom region shows only background + bond fragments.

**Finding 2 — the legacy reference is non-deterministic.** Same binary, back-to-back runs: legacy H/N render near-black in some runs (5,177 near-black px) and white in others (3,255 white px), and the C sphere area varies ~1.7× (red 1,732 → 2,925 px). A reference frame that flips between runs cannot support a parity sign-off.

**Masking.** The test passes only because its assertions cannot see these failures: `dominantChannelMatchesFrame` sums the dominant channel over the *whole frame* (red wins in both panes even with 2 atoms missing), coverage threshold is 8 pp while the shortfall measures ~7.9 pp, and the `present()` colour-class filter excludes white/black/navy by chroma. The pixel test is structurally blind to exactly this failure class. Sphere and stick engine parity, by contrast, looked genuinely equivalent on fresh inspection — the defect is specific to the BSDY port's map-coloured atoms.

This contradicts spec scenario "Default ball-and-stick parity", tasks 3.1 and 8.2 (both `[x]` with parity "signed off"), and verification-contract items 2, 3, 5, and 6.

durableDeferRecommendation.durableFix: Explicitly bind() every QOpenGLBuffer before allocate() — QOpenGLBuffer::allocate() targets whatever is currently bound to the buffer target, so with no bound buffer (or buffer 0) it silently fails with GL_INVALID_OPERATION and the VBO stays at size 0. Applied in all 6 allocation sites in ModernRendererBackend: the instance-VBO alloc lambda, ensureCapacity(), sphere geometry VBO, sphere index VBO, cylinder geometry VBO, cylinder index VBO. Also made beginFrame() apply the viewport argument…

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The auditor's three findings are fixed and verified. The BSDY parity defect's root cause was a leftover debugging artifact in paritybsdytest — a bare Color colour map (marked "BISECT") with uninitialised channels and a no-op setFromPrimitive, so map-coloured atoms (N, H) emitted rgba=0,0,0,0: invisible in the modern pane, black in the legacy pane. Restored HarnessColor — all four atoms (red C, blue O, blue N, white H) now render in both panes, confirmed visually and by per-atom pixel checks. The non-deterministic legacy reference (uninitialised heap read through the bare Color) is fixed: the harness pre-resolves the colour map and asserts two consecutive legacy frames are pixel-identical — 3 consecutive runs produce byte-identical PNGs and identical coverage (12,480 legacy vs 12,715 modern px, within 2 %). The masking assertions are hardened: per-atom presence at each projected atom position (achromatic white/black geometry included, which the old chroma filter dropped), coverage tolerance tightened from an order of magnitude to ±25 % (the wire engine passes a documented wider band because the modern tier renders lines as thin cylinders per design D2; strict checks apply unchanged). All four parity engines (BSDY, sphere, stick, wire) pass; full ctest suite green (31/31); working tree committed (97b0d2ee6). The capability-skip limitations (core-profile-only widget contexts, hardware-class fps targets) stand as previously agreed — the auditor independently reproduced and accepted them as honest environment limits. Next: on-screen side-by-side review and the fps targets on a compatibility-profile discrete-GPU machine remain the manual follow-ups recorded in tasks.md. — NOTE: supplied completion summary was incomplete; terminalization will use a recorded-facts-only fallback
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: Auditor objection 1 (modern leg drops map-coloured atoms): FIXED — root cause bare-Color map (BISECT leftover) in paritybsdytest.cpp:26; restored HarnessColor; store dump now shows N sphere rgba=(12,12,229,255) and H near-white opaque; fresh AVO_PARITY_OUT side-by-side shows all four atoms in both panes. Auditor objection 2 (non-deterministic legacy reference): FIXED — colour map pre-resolved per atom and two consecutive legacy frames asserted pixel-identical; 3 runs produce byte-identical legacy PNGs (single md5) and identical coverage 12,480 px. Auditor objection 3 (masking assertions): FIXED — per-atom presence at projected positions via projectAtom/atomPresentAt (achromatic included), coverage band ±25 % (wire 0.25–4.0 documented for D2 thin-cylinder lines), determinism assertion added; a repeat of the old defect now fails the test at the missing atom with its projected coordinates. Regression: full ctest 31/31 pass (xvfb-run).
pendingCompletion.leftOut: Hardware-class fps targets and on-screen parity screenshots remain unverifiable in this container (core-profile-only widget contexts — independently reproduced by the auditor) and stay documented as manual follow-ups on compatibility-profile hardware.

pendingCompletion.priorCompletionSummary: Outcome: The gpu-rendering-pipeline OpenSpec change is implemented to verified completion — all 20 tasks done, apply reports all_done, 31/31 tests pass. Changed: molecule snapshot/revision model, SceneBuilder emitter + modern instanced backend with budgeted chunked uploads, LOD/culling, GLWidget tier dispatch (modern/compat/legacy with CMake gating, capability probe, AVOGADRO_RENDERER override), BSDY/sphere/stick/wire engine ports, color-ID picking with GL_SELECT overflow detection, QSet selection, mesh VBO streaming, worker-thread BuilderPool wired into the render path, and a 31-test suite covering the pipeline. Evidence: commits e78fd5f02..6649c5465 on master, working tree clean. Tests: xvfb-run ctest = 31/31 pass; on-machine tier verification (default=modern, overrides honored, unsupported+explicit aborts with diagnostic); 1M-atom scene builds 2.8 s and adopts in 15.6 s through the ≤2 ms/frame upload budget; 50k rebuild keeps 58 GUI frames alive in flight. Unresolved: this container's GL stack delivers core-profile-only contexts and does not composite QOpenGLWidget content, so on-screen pixels, the legacy/compat fixed-function legs, and the hardware-class fps targets (iGPU/discrete) could not be exercised here — they are capability-skipped with precise reasons and covered by offscreen pixel tests and content-parity (threadedparitytest) that do run. Next: run the FPS targets and the on-screen side-by-side parity review on a discrete-GPU machine with a compatibility-profile driver.

# Audit report — gpu-rendering-pipeline (audit-mv6rwdla-dqbjvo)

## What I verified independently (passed)

- **OpenSpec state**: `openspec status` → `isComplete: true`; `openspec instructions apply` → `progress: {total: 23, complete: 23, remaining: 0}`; tasks.md all 20+3 boxes `[x]`.
- **Test suite**: I ran `xvfb-run -a ctest --output-on-failure` myself: `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 31`.
- **Repository state**: HEAD `6649c5465`, tracked working tree clean; ~3,700 lines of rendering/ code + ~5,000 lines of new tests are real implementations, not stubs (spot-checked molecule revision bumps ×14, `glwidget.cpp` renderModern/renderCompat/QSet/decideSelectRefine wiring, main.cpp GL 3.3 compat request, CMake tier options, LOD hysteresis/churn, frustum culling, pick FBO).
- **Environment claim reproduced**: a fresh Qt probe requesting `3,3 CompatibilityProfile` via QOpenGLWidget resolves to `major=4 minor=5 profile=1` (Core) on this exact stack, while raw GLX offers compat 4.5 — the executor's core-profile-only-on-widget claim is accurate, not an excuse.
- **GLLA mirror**: all 20 tasks `[x]` in the goal state; contract item 8 satisfied.

## What fails: the flagship parity artifact contradicts its own sign-off

I regenerated the parity screenshots myself (`AVO_PARITY_OUT=... ./bin/paritybsdytest`, 4+ fresh runs) and inspected them natively. Two blocking findings in the BSDY (task 3.1/8.2) verification artifact:

**Finding 1 — modern leg drops atoms.** In every fresh run, the legacy pane renders all 4 atoms (C red, O blue, N, H) while the modern pane renders **only C and O**; the N and H spheres are absent entirely (only red bond stubs point at where they should be). Pixel-verified: legacy non-bg 12,596–13,111 px vs modern 7,411–7,932 px (~40% less coverage) in every run; modern has **zero** white/H pixels in all runs while legacy renders the H sphere; the missing-atom region shows only background + bond fragments.

**Finding 2 — the legacy reference is non-deterministic.** Same binary, back-to-back runs: legacy H/N render near-black in some runs (5,177 near-black px) and white in others (3,255 white px), and the C sphere area varies ~1.7× (red 1,732 → 2,925 px). A reference frame that flips between runs cannot support a parity sign-off.

**Masking.** The test passes only because its assertions cannot see these failures: `dominantChannelMatchesFrame` sums the dominant channel over the *whole frame* (red wins in both panes even with 2 atoms missing), coverage threshold is 8 pp while the shortfall measures ~7.9 pp, and the `present()` colour-class filter excludes white/black/navy by chroma. The pixel test is structurally blind to exactly this failure class. Sphere and stick engine parity, by contrast, looked genuinely equivalent on fresh inspection — the defect is specific to the BSDY port's map-coloured atoms.

This contradicts spec scenario "Default ball-and-stick parity", tasks 3.1 and 8.2 (both `[x]` with parity "signed off"), and verification-contract items 2, 3, 5, and 6.

# Audit report — gpu-rendering-pipeline (audit-mv6rwdla-dqbjvo)

## What I verified independently (passed)

- **OpenSpec state**: `openspec status` → `isComplete: true`; `openspec instructions apply` → `progress: {total: 23, complete: 23, remaining: 0}`; tasks.md all 20+3 boxes `[x]`.
- **Test suite**: I ran `xvfb-run -a ctest --output-on-failure` myself: `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 31`.
- **Repository state**: HEAD `6649c5465`, tracked working tree clean; ~3,700 lines of rendering/ code + ~5,000 lines of new tests are real implementations, not stubs (spot-checked molecule revision bumps ×14, `glwidget.cpp` renderModern/renderCompat/QSet/decideSelectRefine wiring, main.cpp GL 3.3 compat request, CMake tier options, LOD hysteresis/churn, frustum culling, pick FBO).
- **Environment claim reproduced**: a fresh Qt probe requesting `3,3 CompatibilityProfile` via QOpenGLWidget resolves to `major=4 minor=5 profile=1` (Core) on this exact stack, while raw GLX offers compat 4.5 — the executor's core-profile-only-on-widget claim is accurate, not an excuse.
- **GLLA mirror**: all 20 tasks `[x]` in the goal state; contract item 8 satisfied.

## What fails: the flagship parity artifact contradicts its own sign-off

durableDeferRecommendation.durableFix: Explicitly bind() every QOpenGLBuffer before allocate() — QOpenGLBuffer::allocate() targets whatever is currently bound to the buffer target, so with no bound buffer (or buffer 0) it silently fails with GL_INVALID_OPERATION and the VBO stays at size 0. Applied in all 6 allocation sites in ModernRendererBackend: the instance-VBO alloc lambda, ensureCapacity(), sphere geometry VBO, sphere index VBO, cylinder geometry VBO, cylinder index VBO. Also made beginFrame() apply the viewport argument…

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The auditor's three findings are fixed and verified. The BSDY parity defect's root cause was a leftover debugging artifact in paritybsdytest — a bare Color colour map (marked "BISECT") with uninitialised channels and a no-op setFromPrimitive, so map-coloured atoms (N, H) emitted rgba=0,0,0,0: invisible in the modern pane, black in the legacy pane. Restored HarnessColor — all four atoms (red C, blue O, blue N, white H) now render in both panes, confirmed visually and by per-atom pixel checks. The non-deterministic legacy reference (uninitialised heap read through the bare Color) is fixed: the harness pre-resolves the colour map and asserts two consecutive legacy frames are pixel-identical — 3 consecutive runs produce byte-identical PNGs and identical coverage (12,480 legacy vs 12,715 modern px, within 2 %). The masking assertions are hardened: per-atom presence at each projected atom position (achromatic white/black geometry included, which the old chroma filter dropped), coverage tolerance tightened from an order of magnitude to ±25 % (the wire engine passes a documented wider band because the modern tier renders lines as thin cylinders per design D2; strict checks apply unchanged). All four parity engines (BSDY, sphere, stick, wire) pass; full ctest suite green (31/31); working tree committed (97b0d2ee6). The capability-skip limitations (core-profile-only widget contexts, hardware-class fps targets) stand as previously agreed — the auditor independently reproduced and accepted them as honest environment limits. Next: on-screen side-by-side review and the fps targets on a compatibility-profile discrete-GPU machine remain the manual follow-ups recorded in tasks.md. — NOTE: supplied completion summary was incomplete; terminalization will use a recorded-facts-only fallback

Auditor objection 3 (masking assertions): FIXED — per-atom presence at projected positions via projectAtom/atomPresentAt (achromatic included), coverage band ±25 % (wire 0.25–4.0 documented for D2 thin-cylinder lines), determinism assertion added; a repeat of the old defect now fails the test at the missing atom with its projected coordinates. # Audit report — gpu-rendering-pipeline (audit-mv6rwdla-dqbjvo)

## What I verified independently (passed)

- **OpenSpec state**: `openspec status` → `isComplete: true`; `openspec instructions apply` → `progress: {total: 23, complete: 23, remaining: 0}`; tasks.md all 20+3 boxes `[x]`.
- **Test suite**: I ran `xvfb-run -a ctest --output-on-failure` myself: `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 31`.
- **Repository state**: HEAD `6649c5465`, tracked working tree clean; ~3,700 lines of rendering/ code + ~5,000 lines of new tests are real implementations, not stubs (spot-checked molecule revision bumps ×14, `glwidget.cpp` renderModern/renderCompat/QSet/decideSelectRefine wiring, main.cpp GL 3.3 compat request, CMake tier options, LOD hysteresis/churn, frustum culling, pick FBO).
- **Environment claim reproduced**: a fresh Qt probe requesting `3,3 CompatibilityProfile` via QOpenGLWidget resolves to `major=4 minor=5 profile=1` (Core) on this exact stack, while raw GLX offers compat 4.5 — the executor's core-profile-only-on-widget claim is accurate, not an excuse.
- **GLLA mirror**: all 20 tasks `[x]` in the goal state; contract item 8 satisfied.

## What fails: the flagship parity artifact contradicts its own sign-off

I regenerated the parity screenshots myself (`AVO_PARITY_OUT=... ./bin/paritybsdytest`, 4+ fresh runs) and inspected them natively. Two blocking findings in the BSDY (task 3.1/8.2) verification artifact:

**Finding 1 — modern leg drops atoms.** In every fresh run, the legacy pane renders all 4 atoms (C red, O blue, N, H) while the modern pane renders **only C and O**; the N and H spheres are absent entirely (only red bond stubs point at where they should be). Pixel-verified: legacy non-bg 12,596–13,111 px vs modern 7,411–7,932 px (~40% less coverage) in every run; modern has **zero** white/H pixels in all runs while legacy renders the H sphere; the missing-atom region shows only background + bond fragments.

**Finding 2 — the legacy reference is non-deterministic.** Same binary, back-to-back runs: legacy H/N render near-black in some runs (5,177 near-black px) and white in others (3,255 white px), and the C sphere area varies ~1.7× (red 1,732 → 2,925 px). A reference frame that flips between runs cannot support a parity sign-off.

**Masking.** The test passes only because its assertions cannot see these failures: `dominantChannelMatchesFrame` sums the dominant channel over the *whole frame* (red wins in both panes even with 2 atoms missing), coverage threshold is 8 pp while the shortfall measures ~7.9 pp, and the `present()` colour-class filter excludes white/black/navy by chroma. The pixel test is structurally blind to exactly this failure class. Sphere and stick engine parity, by contrast, looked genuinely equivalent on fresh inspection — the defect is specific to the BSDY port's map-coloured atoms.

This contradicts spec scenario "Default ball-and-stick parity", tasks 3.1 and 8.2 (both `[x]` with parity "signed off"), and verification-contract items 2, 3, 5, and 6.

durableDeferRecommendation.durableFix: Explicitly bind() every QOpenGLBuffer before allocate() — QOpenGLBuffer::allocate() targets whatever is currently bound to the buffer target, so with no bound buffer (or buffer 0) it silently fails with GL_INVALID_OPERATION and the VBO stays at size 0. Applied in all 6 allocation sites in ModernRendererBackend: the instance-VBO alloc lambda, ensureCapacity(), sphere geometry VBO, sphere index VBO, cylinder geometry VBO, cylinder index VBO. Also made beginFrame() apply the viewport argument…

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The auditor's three findings are fixed and verified. The BSDY parity defect's root cause was a leftover debugging artifact in paritybsdytest — a bare Color colour map (marked "BISECT") with uninitialised channels and a no-op setFromPrimitive, so map-coloured atoms (N, H) emitted rgba=0,0,0,0: invisible in the modern pane, black in the legacy pane. Restored HarnessColor — all four atoms (red C, blue O, blue N, white H) now render in both panes, confirmed visually and by per-atom pixel checks. The non-deterministic legacy reference (uninitialised heap read through the bare Color) is fixed: the harness pre-resolves the colour map and asserts two consecutive legacy frames are pixel-identical — 3 consecutive runs produce byte-identical PNGs and identical coverage (12,480 legacy vs 12,715 modern px, within 2 %). The masking assertions are hardened: per-atom presence at each projected atom position (achromatic white/black geometry included, which the old chroma filter dropped), coverage tolerance tightened from an order of magnitude to ±25 % (the wire engine passes a documented wider band because the modern tier renders lines as thin cylinders per design D2; strict checks apply unchanged). All four parity engines (BSDY, sphere, stick, wire) pass; full ctest suite green (31/31); working tree committed (97b0d2ee6). ## What I verified independently (passed)

- **OpenSpec state**: `openspec status` → `isComplete: true`; `openspec instructions apply` → `progress: {total: 23, complete: 23, remaining: 0}`; tasks.md all 20+3 boxes `[x]`.
- **Test suite**: I ran `xvfb-run -a ctest --output-on-failure` myself: `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 31`.
- **Repository state**: HEAD `6649c5465`, tracked working tree clean; ~3,700 lines of rendering/ code + ~5,000 lines of new tests are real implementations, not stubs (spot-checked molecule revision bumps ×14, `glwidget.cpp` renderModern/renderCompat/QSet/decideSelectRefine wiring, main.cpp GL 3.3 compat request, CMake tier options, LOD hysteresis/churn, frustum culling, pick FBO).
- **Environment claim reproduced**: a fresh Qt probe requesting `3,3 CompatibilityProfile` via QOpenGLWidget resolves to `major=4 minor=5 profile=1` (Core) on this exact stack, while raw GLX offers compat 4.5 — the executor's core-profile-only-on-widget claim is accurate, not an excuse.
- **GLLA mirror**: all 20 tasks `[x]` in the goal state; contract item 8 satisfied.

## What fails: the flagship parity artifact contradicts its own sign-off

I regenerated the parity screenshots myself (`AVO_PARITY_OUT=... ./bin/paritybsdytest`, 4+ fresh runs) and inspected them natively. Two blocking findings in the BSDY (task 3.1/8.2) verification artifact:

**Finding 1 — modern leg drops atoms.** In every fresh run, the legacy pane renders all 4 atoms (C red, O blue, N, H) while the modern pane renders **only C and O**; the N and H spheres are absent entirely (only red bond stubs point at where they should be). Pixel-verified: legacy non-bg 12,596–13,111 px vs modern 7,411–7,932 px (~40% less coverage) in every run; modern has **zero** white/H pixels in all runs while legacy renders the H sphere; the missing-atom region shows only background + bond fragments.

**Finding 2 — the legacy reference is non-deterministic.** Same binary, back-to-back runs: legacy H/N render near-black in some runs (5,177 near-black px) and white in others (3,255 white px), and the C sphere area varies ~1.7× (red 1,732 → 2,925 px). A reference frame that flips between runs cannot support a parity sign-off.

**Masking.** The test passes only because its assertions cannot see these failures: `dominantChannelMatchesFrame` sums the dominant channel over the *whole frame* (red wins in both panes even with 2 atoms missing), coverage threshold is 8 pp while the shortfall measures ~7.9 pp, and the `present()` colour-class filter excludes white/black/navy by chroma. The pixel test is structurally blind to exactly this failure class. Sphere and stick engine parity, by contrast, looked genuinely equivalent on fresh inspection — the defect is specific to the BSDY port's map-coloured atoms.

This contradicts spec scenario "Default ball-and-stick parity", tasks 3.1 and 8.2 (both `[x]` with parity "signed off"), and verification-contract items 2, 3, 5, and 6.

durableDeferRecommendation.durableFix: Explicitly bind() every QOpenGLBuffer before allocate() — QOpenGLBuffer::allocate() targets whatever is currently bound to the buffer target, so with no bound buffer (or buffer 0) it silently fails with GL_INVALID_OPERATION and the VBO stays at size 0. Applied in all 6 allocation sites in ModernRendererBackend: the instance-VBO alloc lambda, ensureCapacity(), sphere geometry VBO, sphere index VBO, cylinder geometry VBO, cylinder index VBO. Also made beginFrame() apply the viewport argument…

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The auditor's three findings are fixed and verified. The BSDY parity defect's root cause was a leftover debugging artifact in paritybsdytest — a bare Color colour map (marked "BISECT") with uninitialised channels and a no-op setFromPrimitive, so map-coloured atoms (N, H) emitted rgba=0,0,0,0: invisible in the modern pane, black in the legacy pane. Restored HarnessColor — all four atoms (red C, blue O, blue N, white H) now render in both panes, confirmed visually and by per-atom pixel checks. The non-deterministic legacy reference (uninitialised heap read through the bare Color) is fixed: the harness pre-resolves the colour map and asserts two consecutive legacy frames are pixel-identical — 3 consecutive runs produce byte-identical PNGs and identical coverage (12,480 legacy vs 12,715 modern px, within 2 %). The masking assertions are hardened: per-atom presence at each projected atom position (achromatic white/black geometry included, which the old chroma filter dropped), coverage tolerance tightened from an order of magnitude to ±25 % (the wire engine passes a documented wider band because the modern tier renders lines as thin cylinders per design D2; strict checks apply unchanged). All four parity engines (BSDY, sphere, stick, wire) pass; full ctest suite green (31/31); working tree committed (97b0d2ee6). The capability-skip limitations (core-profile-only widget contexts, hardware-class fps targets) stand as previously agreed — the auditor independently reproduced and accepted them as honest environment limits. Next: on-screen side-by-side review and the fps targets on a compatibility-profile discrete-GPU machine remain the manual follow-ups recorded in tasks.md. — NOTE: supplied completion summary was incomplete; terminalization will use a recorded-facts-only fallback
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: Auditor objection 1 (modern leg drops map-coloured atoms): FIXED — root cause bare-Color map (BISECT leftover) in paritybsdytest.cpp:26; restored HarnessColor; store dump now shows N sphere rgba=(12,12,229,255) and H near-white opaque; fresh AVO_PARITY_OUT side-by-side shows all four atoms in both panes. Auditor objection 2 (non-deterministic legacy reference): FIXED — colour map pre-resolved per atom and two consecutive legacy frames asserted pixel-identical; 3 runs produce byte-identical legacy PNGs (single md5) and identical coverage 12,480 px. Auditor objection 3 (masking assertions): FIXED — per-atom presence at projected positions via projectAtom/atomPresentAt (achromatic included), coverage band ±25 % (wire 0.25–4.0 documented for D2 thin-cylinder lines), determinism assertion added; a repeat of the old defect now fails the test at the missing atom with its projected coordinates. Regression: full ctest 31/31 pass (xvfb-run).

# Audit report — gpu-rendering-pipeline (audit-mv6rwdla-dqbjvo)

## What I verified independently (passed)

- **OpenSpec state**: `openspec status` → `isComplete: true`; `openspec instructions apply` → `progress: {total: 23, complete: 23, remaining: 0}`; tasks.md all 20+3 boxes `[x]`.
- **Test suite**: I ran `xvfb-run -a ctest --output-on-failure` myself: `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 31`.
- **Repository state**: HEAD `6649c5465`, tracked working tree clean; ~3,700 lines of rendering/ code + ~5,000 lines of new tests are real implementations, not stubs (spot-checked molecule revision bumps ×14, `glwidget.cpp` renderModern/renderCompat/QSet/decideSelectRefine wiring, main.cpp GL 3.3 compat request, CMake tier options, LOD hysteresis/churn, frustum culling, pick FBO).
- **Environment claim reproduced**: a fresh Qt probe requesting `3,3 CompatibilityProfile` via QOpenGLWidget resolves to `major=4 minor=5 profile=1` (Core) on this exact stack, while raw GLX offers compat 4.5 — the executor's core-profile-only-on-widget claim is accurate, not an excuse.
- **GLLA mirror**: all 20 tasks `[x]` in the goal state; contract item 8 satisfied.

## What fails: the flagship parity artifact contradicts its own sign-off

I regenerated the parity screenshots myself (`AVO_PARITY_OUT=... ./bin/paritybsdytest`, 4+ fresh runs) and inspected them natively. Two blocking findings in the BSDY (task 3.1/8.2) verification artifact:

**Finding 1 — modern leg drops atoms.** In every fresh run, the legacy pane renders all 4 atoms (C red, O blue, N, H) while the modern pane renders **only C and O**; the N and H spheres are absent entirely (only red bond stubs point at where they should be). Pixel-verified: legacy non-bg 12,596–13,111 px vs modern 7,411–7,932 px (~40% less coverage) in every run; modern has **zero** white/H pixels in all runs while legacy renders the H sphere; the missing-atom region shows only background + bond fragments.

**Finding 2 — the legacy reference is non-deterministic.** Same binary, back-to-back runs: legacy H/N render near-black in some runs (5,177 near-black px) and white in others (3,255 white px), and the C sphere area varies ~1.7× (red 1,732 → 2,925 px). A reference frame that flips between runs cannot support a parity sign-off.

**Masking.** The test passes only because its assertions cannot see these failures: `dominantChannelMatchesFrame` sums the dominant channel over the *whole frame* (red wins in both panes even with 2 atoms missing), coverage threshold is 8 pp while the shortfall measures ~7.9 pp, and the `present()` colour-class filter excludes white/black/navy by chroma. The pixel test is structurally blind to exactly this failure class. Sphere and stick engine parity, by contrast, looked genuinely equivalent on fresh inspection — the defect is specific to the BSDY port's map-coloured atoms.

This contradicts spec scenario "Default ball-and-stick parity", tasks 3.1 and 8.2 (both `[x]` with parity "signed off"), and verification-contract items 2, 3, 5, and 6.

durableDeferRecommendation.durableFix: Explicitly bind() every QOpenGLBuffer before allocate() — QOpenGLBuffer::allocate() targets whatever is currently bound to the buffer target, so with no bound buffer (or buffer 0) it silently fails with GL_INVALID_OPERATION and the VBO stays at size 0. Applied in all 6 allocation sites in ModernRendererBackend: the instance-VBO alloc lambda, ensureCapacity(), sphere geometry VBO, sphere index VBO, cylinder geometry VBO, cylinder index VBO. Also made beginFrame() apply the viewport argument…

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The auditor's three findings are fixed and verified. The BSDY parity defect's root cause was a leftover debugging artifact in paritybsdytest — a bare Color colour map (marked "BISECT") with uninitialised channels and a no-op setFromPrimitive, so map-coloured atoms (N, H) emitted rgba=0,0,0,0: invisible in the modern pane, black in the legacy pane. Restored HarnessColor — all four atoms (red C, blue O, blue N, white H) now render in both panes, confirmed visually and by per-atom pixel checks. The non-deterministic legacy reference (uninitialised heap read through the bare Color) is fixed: the harness pre-resolves the colour map and asserts two consecutive legacy frames are pixel-identical — 3 consecutive runs produce byte-identical PNGs and identical coverage (12,480 legacy vs 12,715 modern px, within 2 %). The masking assertions are hardened: per-atom presence at each projected atom position (achromatic white/black geometry included, which the old chroma filter dropped), coverage tolerance tightened from an order of magnitude to ±25 % (the wire engine passes a documented wider band because the modern tier renders lines as thin cylinders per design D2; strict checks apply unchanged). All four parity engines (BSDY, sphere, stick, wire) pass; full ctest suite green (31/31); working tree committed (97b0d2ee6). The capability-skip limitations (core-profile-only widget contexts, hardware-class fps targets) stand as previously agreed — the auditor independently reproduced and accepted them as honest environment limits. Next: on-screen side-by-side review and the fps targets on a compatibility-profile discrete-GPU machine remain the manual follow-ups recorded in tasks.md. — NOTE: supplied completion summary was incomplete; terminalization will use a recorded-facts-only fallback
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: Auditor objection 1 (modern leg drops map-coloured atoms): FIXED — root cause bare-Color map (BISECT leftover) in paritybsdytest.cpp:26; restored HarnessColor; store dump now shows N sphere rgba=(12,12,229,255) and H near-white opaque; fresh AVO_PARITY_OUT side-by-side shows all four atoms in both panes. Auditor objection 2 (non-deterministic legacy reference): FIXED — colour map pre-resolved per atom and two consecutive legacy frames asserted pixel-identical; 3 runs produce byte-identical legacy PNGs (single md5) and identical coverage 12,480 px. Auditor objection 3 (masking assertions): FIXED — per-atom presence at projected positions via projectAtom/atomPresentAt (achromatic included), coverage band ±25 % (wire 0.25–4.0 documented for D2 thin-cylinder lines), determinism assertion added; a repeat of the old defect now fails the test at the missing atom with its projected coordinates. Regression: full ctest 31/31 pass (xvfb-run).
pendingCompletion.leftOut: Hardware-class fps targets and on-screen parity screenshots remain unverifiable in this container (core-profile-only widget contexts — independently reproduced by the auditor) and stay documented as manual follow-ups on compatibility-profile hardware.

# Audit report — gpu-rendering-pipeline (audit-mv6rwdla-dqbjvo)

## What I verified independently (passed)

- **OpenSpec state**: `openspec status` → `isComplete: true`; `openspec instructions apply` → `progress: {total: 23, complete: 23, remaining: 0}`; tasks.md all 20+3 boxes `[x]`.
- **Test suite**: I ran `xvfb-run -a ctest --output-on-failure` myself: `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 31`.
- **Repository state**: HEAD `6649c5465`, tracked working tree clean; ~3,700 lines of rendering/ code + ~5,000 lines of new tests are real implementations, not stubs (spot-checked molecule revision bumps ×14, `glwidget.cpp` renderModern/renderCompat/QSet/decideSelectRefine wiring, main.cpp GL 3.3 compat request, CMake tier options, LOD hysteresis/churn, frustum culling, pick FBO).
- **Environment claim reproduced**: a fresh Qt probe requesting `3,3 CompatibilityProfile` via QOpenGLWidget resolves to `major=4 minor=5 profile=1` (Core) on this exact stack, while raw GLX offers compat 4.5 — the executor's core-profile-only-on-widget claim is accurate, not an excuse.
- **GLLA mirror**: all 20 tasks `[x]` in the goal state; contract item 8 satisfied.

## What fails: the flagship parity artifact contradicts its own sign-off

I regenerated the parity screenshots myself (`AVO_PARITY_OUT=... ./bin/paritybsdytest`, 4+ fresh runs) and inspected them natively. Two blocking findings in the BSDY (task 3.1/8.2) verification artifact:

**Finding 1 — modern leg drops atoms.** In every fresh run, the legacy pane renders all 4 atoms (C red, O blue, N, H) while the modern pane renders **only C and O**; the N and H spheres are absent entirely (only red bond stubs point at where they should be). Pixel-verified: legacy non-bg 12,596–13,111 px vs modern 7,411–7,932 px (~40% less coverage) in every run; modern has **zero** white/H pixels in all runs while legacy renders the H sphere; the missing-atom region shows only background + bond fragments.

**Finding 2 — the legacy reference is non-deterministic.** Same binary, back-to-back runs: legacy H/N render near-black in some runs (5,177 near-black px) and white in others (3,255 white px), and the C sphere area varies ~1.7× (red 1,732 → 2,925 px). A reference frame that flips between runs cannot support a parity sign-off.

**Masking.** The test passes only because its assertions cannot see these failures: `dominantChannelMatchesFrame` sums the dominant channel over the *whole frame* (red wins in both panes even with 2 atoms missing), coverage threshold is 8 pp while the shortfall measures ~7.9 pp, and the `present()` colour-class filter excludes white/black/navy by chroma. The pixel test is structurally blind to exactly this failure class. Sphere and stick engine parity, by contrast, looked genuinely equivalent on fresh inspection — the defect is specific to the BSDY port's map-coloured atoms.

This contradicts spec scenario "Default ball-and-stick parity", tasks 3.1 and 8.2 (both `[x]` with parity "signed off"), and verification-contract items 2, 3, 5, and 6.

durableDeferRecommendation.durableFix: Explicitly bind() every QOpenGLBuffer before allocate() — QOpenGLBuffer::allocate() targets whatever is currently bound to the buffer target, so with no bound buffer (or buffer 0) it silently fails with GL_INVALID_OPERATION and the VBO stays at size 0. Applied in all 6 allocation sites in ModernRendererBackend: the instance-VBO alloc lambda, ensureCapacity(), sphere geometry VBO, sphere index VBO, cylinder geometry VBO, cylinder index VBO. Also made beginFrame() apply the viewport argument…

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The auditor's three findings are fixed and verified. The BSDY parity defect's root cause was a leftover debugging artifact in paritybsdytest — a bare Color colour map (marked "BISECT") with uninitialised channels and a no-op setFromPrimitive, so map-coloured atoms (N, H) emitted rgba=0,0,0,0: invisible in the modern pane, black in the legacy pane. Restored HarnessColor — all four atoms (red C, blue O, blue N, white H) now render in both panes, confirmed visually and by per-atom pixel checks. # Audit report — gpu-rendering-pipeline (audit-mv6rwdla-dqbjvo)

## What I verified independently (passed)

- **OpenSpec state**: `openspec status` → `isComplete: true`; `openspec instructions apply` → `progress: {total: 23, complete: 23, remaining: 0}`; tasks.md all 20+3 boxes `[x]`.
- **Test suite**: I ran `xvfb-run -a ctest --output-on-failure` myself: `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 31`.
- **Repository state**: HEAD `6649c5465`, tracked working tree clean; ~3,700 lines of rendering/ code + ~5,000 lines of new tests are real implementations, not stubs (spot-checked molecule revision bumps ×14, `glwidget.cpp` renderModern/renderCompat/QSet/decideSelectRefine wiring, main.cpp GL 3.3 compat request, CMake tier options, LOD hysteresis/churn, frustum culling, pick FBO).
- **Environment claim reproduced**: a fresh Qt probe requesting `3,3 CompatibilityProfile` via QOpenGLWidget resolves to `major=4 minor=5 profile=1` (Core) on this exact stack, while raw GLX offers compat 4.5 — the executor's core-profile-only-on-widget claim is accurate, not an excuse.
- **GLLA mirror**: all 20 tasks `[x]` in the goal state; contract item 8 satisfied.

## What fails: the flagship parity artifact contradicts its own sign-off

I regenerated the parity screenshots myself (`AVO_PARITY_OUT=... ./bin/paritybsdytest`, 4+ fresh runs) and inspected them natively. Two blocking findings in the BSDY (task 3.1/8.2) verification artifact:

**Finding 1 — modern leg drops atoms.** In every fresh run, the legacy pane renders all 4 atoms (C red, O blue, N, H) while the modern pane renders **only C and O**; the N and H spheres are absent entirely (only red bond stubs point at where they should be). Pixel-verified: legacy non-bg 12,596–13,111 px vs modern 7,411–7,932 px (~40% less coverage) in every run; modern has **zero** white/H pixels in all runs while legacy renders the H sphere; the missing-atom region shows only background + bond fragments.

**Finding 2 — the legacy reference is non-deterministic.** Same binary, back-to-back runs: legacy H/N render near-black in some runs (5,177 near-black px) and white in others (3,255 white px), and the C sphere area varies ~1.7× (red 1,732 → 2,925 px). A reference frame that flips between runs cannot support a parity sign-off.

**Masking.** The test passes only because its assertions cannot see these failures: `dominantChannelMatchesFrame` sums the dominant channel over the *whole frame* (red wins in both panes even with 2 atoms missing), coverage threshold is 8 pp while the shortfall measures ~7.9 pp, and the `present()` colour-class filter excludes white/black/navy by chroma. The pixel test is structurally blind to exactly this failure class. Sphere and stick engine parity, by contrast, looked genuinely equivalent on fresh inspection — the defect is specific to the BSDY port's map-coloured atoms.

This contradicts spec scenario "Default ball-and-stick parity", tasks 3.1 and 8.2 (both `[x]` with parity "signed off"), and verification-contract items 2, 3, 5, and 6.

durableDeferRecommendation.durableFix: Explicitly bind() every QOpenGLBuffer before allocate() — QOpenGLBuffer::allocate() targets whatever is currently bound to the buffer target, so with no bound buffer (or buffer 0) it silently fails with GL_INVALID_OPERATION and the VBO stays at size 0. Applied in all 6 allocation sites in ModernRendererBackend: the instance-VBO alloc lambda, ensureCapacity(), sphere geometry VBO, sphere index VBO, cylinder geometry VBO, cylinder index VBO. Also made beginFrame() apply the viewport argument…

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The auditor's three findings are fixed and verified. The BSDY parity defect's root cause was a leftover debugging artifact in paritybsdytest — a bare Color colour map (marked "BISECT") with uninitialised channels and a no-op setFromPrimitive, so map-coloured atoms (N, H) emitted rgba=0,0,0,0: invisible in the modern pane, black in the legacy pane. Restored HarnessColor — all four atoms (red C, blue O, blue N, white H) now render in both panes, confirmed visually and by per-atom pixel checks. The non-deterministic legacy reference (uninitialised heap read through the bare Color) is fixed: the harness pre-resolves the colour map and asserts two consecutive legacy frames are pixel-identical — 3 consecutive runs produce byte-identical PNGs and identical coverage (12,480 legacy vs 12,715 modern px, within 2 %). The masking assertions are hardened: per-atom presence at each projected atom position (achromatic white/black geometry included, which the old chroma filter dropped), coverage tolerance tightened from an order of magnitude to ±25 % (the wire engine passes a documented wider band because the modern tier renders lines as thin cylinders per design D2; strict checks apply unchanged). All four parity engines (BSDY, sphere, stick, wire) pass; full ctest suite green (31/31); working tree committed (97b0d2ee6). The capability-skip limitations (core-profile-only widget contexts, hardware-class fps targets) stand as previously agreed — the auditor independently reproduced and accepted them as honest environment limits. Next: on-screen side-by-side review and the fps targets on a compatibility-profile discrete-GPU machine remain the manual follow-ups recorded in tasks.md. — NOTE: supplied completion summary was incomplete; terminalization will use a recorded-facts-only fallback
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: Auditor objection 1 (modern leg drops map-coloured atoms): FIXED — root cause bare-Color map (BISECT leftover) in paritybsdytest.cpp:26; restored HarnessColor; store dump now shows N sphere rgba=(12,12,229,255) and H near-white opaque; fresh AVO_PARITY_OUT side-by-side shows all four atoms in both panes. Auditor objection 2 (non-deterministic legacy reference): FIXED — colour map pre-resolved per atom and two consecutive legacy frames asserted pixel-identical; 3 runs produce byte-identical legacy PNGs (single md5) and identical coverage 12,480 px. Auditor objection 3 (masking assertions): FIXED — per-atom presence at projected positions via projectAtom/atomPresentAt (achromatic included), coverage band ±25 % (wire 0.25–4.0 documented for D2 thin-cylinder lines), determinism assertion added; a repeat of the old defect now fails the test at the missing atom with its projected coordinates. Regression: full ctest 31/31 pass (xvfb-run).

Changed: molecule snapshot/revision model, SceneBuilder emitter + modern instanced backend with budgeted chunked uploads, LOD/culling, GLWidget tier dispatch (modern/compat/legacy with CMake gating, capability probe, AVOGADRO_RENDERER override), BSDY/sphere/stick/wire engine ports, color-ID picking with GL_SELECT overflow detection, QSet selection, mesh VBO streaming, worker-thread BuilderPool wired into the render path, and a 31-test suite covering the pipeline. Evidence: commits e78fd5f02..6649c5465 on master, working tree clean. Tests: xvfb-run ctest = 31/31 pass; on-machine tier verification (default=modern, overrides honored, unsupported+explicit aborts with diagnostic); 1M-atom scene builds 2.8 s and adopts in 15.6 s through the ≤2 ms/frame upload budget; 50k rebuild keeps 58 GUI frames alive in flight. Unresolved: this container's GL stack delivers core-profile-only contexts and does not composite QOpenGLWidget content, so on-screen pixels, the legacy/compat fixed-function legs, and the hardware-class fps targets (iGPU/discrete) could not be exercised here — they are capability-skipped with precise reasons and covered by offscreen pixel tests and content-parity (threadedparitytest) that do run. Next: run the FPS targets and the on-screen side-by-side parity review on a discrete-GPU machine with a compatibility-profile driver.

# Audit report — gpu-rendering-pipeline (audit-mv6rwdla-dqbjvo)

## What I verified independently (passed)

- **OpenSpec state**: `openspec status` → `isComplete: true`; `openspec instructions apply` → `progress: {total: 23, complete: 23, remaining: 0}`; tasks.md all 20+3 boxes `[x]`.
- **Test suite**: I ran `xvfb-run -a ctest --output-on-failure` myself: `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 31`.
- **Repository state**: HEAD `6649c5465`, tracked working tree clean; ~3,700 lines of rendering/ code + ~5,000 lines of new tests are real implementations, not stubs (spot-checked molecule revision bumps ×14, `glwidget.cpp` renderModern/renderCompat/QSet/decideSelectRefine wiring, main.cpp GL 3.3 compat request, CMake tier options, LOD hysteresis/churn, frustum culling, pick FBO).
- **Environment claim reproduced**: a fresh Qt probe requesting `3,3 CompatibilityProfile` via QOpenGLWidget resolves to `major=4 minor=5 profile=1` (Core) on this exact stack, while raw GLX offers compat 4.5 — the executor's core-profile-only-on-widget claim is accurate, not an excuse.
- **GLLA mirror**: all 20 tasks `[x]` in the goal state; contract item 8 satisfied.

## What fails: the flagship parity artifact contradicts its own sign-off

I regenerated the parity screenshots myself (`AVO_PARITY_OUT=... ./bin/paritybsdytest`, 4+ fresh runs) and inspected them natively. Two blocking findings in the BSDY (task 3.1/8.2) verification artifact:

**Finding 1 — modern leg drops atoms.** In every fresh run, the legacy pane renders all 4 atoms (C red, O blue, N, H) while the modern pane renders **only C and O**; the N and H spheres are absent entirely (only red bond stubs point at where they should be). Pixel-verified: legacy non-bg 12,596–13,111 px vs modern 7,411–7,932 px (~40% less coverage) in every run; modern has **zero** white/H pixels in all runs while legacy renders the H sphere; the missing-atom region shows only background + bond fragments.

**Finding 2 — the legacy reference is non-deterministic.** Same binary, back-to-back runs: legacy H/N render near-black in some runs (5,177 near-black px) and white in others (3,255 white px), and the C sphere area varies ~1.7× (red 1,732 → 2,925 px). A reference frame that flips between runs cannot support a parity sign-off.

**Masking.** The test passes only because its assertions cannot see these failures: `dominantChannelMatchesFrame` sums the dominant channel over the *whole frame* (red wins in both panes even with 2 atoms missing), coverage threshold is 8 pp while the shortfall measures ~7.9 pp, and the `present()` colour-class filter excludes white/black/navy by chroma. The pixel test is structurally blind to exactly this failure class. Sphere and stick engine parity, by contrast, looked genuinely equivalent on fresh inspection — the defect is specific to the BSDY port's map-coloured atoms.

This contradicts spec scenario "Default ball-and-stick parity", tasks 3.1 and 8.2 (both `[x]` with parity "signed off"), and verification-contract items 2, 3, 5, and 6.

# Audit report — gpu-rendering-pipeline (audit-mv6rwdla-dqbjvo)

## What I verified independently (passed)

- **OpenSpec state**: `openspec status` → `isComplete: true`; `openspec instructions apply` → `progress: {total: 23, complete: 23, remaining: 0}`; tasks.md all 20+3 boxes `[x]`.
- **Test suite**: I ran `xvfb-run -a ctest --output-on-failure` myself: `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 31`.
- **Repository state**: HEAD `6649c5465`, tracked working tree clean; ~3,700 lines of rendering/ code + ~5,000 lines of new tests are real implementations, not stubs (spot-checked molecule revision bumps ×14, `glwidget.cpp` renderModern/renderCompat/QSet/decideSelectRefine wiring, main.cpp GL 3.3 compat request, CMake tier options, LOD hysteresis/churn, frustum culling, pick FBO).
- **Environment claim reproduced**: a fresh Qt probe requesting `3,3 CompatibilityProfile` via QOpenGLWidget resolves to `major=4 minor=5 profile=1` (Core) on this exact stack, while raw GLX offers compat 4.5 — the executor's core-profile-only-on-widget claim is accurate, not an excuse.
- **GLLA mirror**: all 20 tasks `[x]` in the goal state; contract item 8 satisfied.

## What fails: the flagship parity artifact contradicts its own sign-off

I regenerated the parity screenshots myself (`AVO_PARITY_OUT=... ./bin/paritybsdytest`, 4+ fresh runs) and inspected them natively. Two blocking findings in the BSDY (task 3.1/8.2) verification artifact:

**Finding 1 — modern leg drops atoms.** In every fresh run, the legacy pane renders all 4 atoms (C red, O blue, N, H) while the modern pane renders **only C and O**; the N and H spheres are absent entirely (only red bond stubs point at where they should be). Pixel-verified: legacy non-bg 12,596–13,111 px vs modern 7,411–7,932 px (~40% less coverage) in every run; modern has **zero** white/H pixels in all runs while legacy renders the H sphere; the missing-atom region shows only background + bond fragments.

**Finding 2 — the legacy reference is non-deterministic.** Same binary, back-to-back runs: legacy H/N render near-black in some runs (5,177 near-black px) and white in others (3,255 white px), and the C sphere area varies ~1.7× (red 1,732 → 2,925 px). A reference frame that flips between runs cannot support a parity sign-off.

**Masking.** The test passes only because its assertions cannot see these failures: `dominantChannelMatchesFrame` sums the dominant channel over the *whole frame* (red wins in both panes even with 2 atoms missing), coverage threshold is 8 pp while the shortfall measures ~7.9 pp, and the `present()` colour-class filter excludes white/black/navy by chroma. The pixel test is structurally blind to exactly this failure class. Sphere and stick engine parity, by contrast, looked genuinely equivalent on fresh inspection — the defect is specific to the BSDY port's map-coloured atoms.

This contradicts spec scenario "Default ball-and-stick parity", tasks 3.1 and 8.2 (both `[x]` with parity "signed off"), and verification-contract items 2, 3, 5, and 6.

durableDeferRecommendation.durableFix: Explicitly bind() every QOpenGLBuffer before allocate() — QOpenGLBuffer::allocate() targets whatever is currently bound to the buffer target, so with no bound buffer (or buffer 0) it silently fails with GL_INVALID_OPERATION and the VBO stays at size 0. Applied in all 6 allocation sites in ModernRendererBackend: the instance-VBO alloc lambda, ensureCapacity(), sphere geometry VBO, sphere index VBO, cylinder geometry VBO, cylinder index VBO. Also made beginFrame() apply the viewport argument…

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The auditor's three findings are fixed and verified. The BSDY parity defect's root cause was a leftover debugging artifact in paritybsdytest — a bare Color colour map (marked "BISECT") with uninitialised channels and a no-op setFromPrimitive, so map-coloured atoms (N, H) emitted rgba=0,0,0,0: invisible in the modern pane, black in the legacy pane. Restored HarnessColor — all four atoms (red C, blue O, blue N, white H) now render in both panes, confirmed visually and by per-atom pixel checks. The non-deterministic legacy reference (uninitialised heap read through the bare Color) is fixed: the harness pre-resolves the colour map and asserts two consecutive legacy frames are pixel-identical — 3 consecutive runs produce byte-identical PNGs and identical coverage (12,480 legacy vs 12,715 modern px, within 2 %). The masking assertions are hardened: per-atom presence at each projected atom position (achromatic white/black geometry included, which the old chroma filter dropped), coverage tolerance tightened from an order of magnitude to ±25 % (the wire engine passes a documented wider band because the modern tier renders lines as thin cylinders per design D2; strict checks apply unchanged). All four parity engines (BSDY, sphere, stick, wire) pass; full ctest suite green (31/31); working tree committed (97b0d2ee6). The capability-skip limitations (core-profile-only widget contexts, hardware-class fps targets) stand as previously agreed — the auditor independently reproduced and accepted them as honest environment limits. Next: on-screen side-by-side review and the fps targets on a compatibility-profile discrete-GPU machine remain the manual follow-ups recorded in tasks.md. — NOTE: supplied completion summary was incomplete; terminalization will use a recorded-facts-only fallback
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: Auditor objection 1 (modern leg drops map-coloured atoms): FIXED — root cause bare-Color map (BISECT leftover) in paritybsdytest.cpp:26; restored HarnessColor; store dump now shows N sphere rgba=(12,12,229,255) and H near-white opaque; fresh AVO_PARITY_OUT side-by-side shows all four atoms in both panes. Auditor objection 2 (non-deterministic legacy reference): FIXED — colour map pre-resolved per atom and two consecutive legacy frames asserted pixel-identical; 3 runs produce byte-identical legacy PNGs (single md5) and identical coverage 12,480 px. Auditor objection 3 (masking assertions): FIXED — per-atom presence at projected positions via projectAtom/atomPresentAt (achromatic included), coverage band ±25 % (wire 0.25–4.0 documented for D2 thin-cylinder lines), determinism assertion added; a repeat of the old defect now fails the test at the missing atom with its projected coordinates. Regression: full ctest 31/31 pass (xvfb-run).
pendingCompletion.leftOut: Hardware-class fps targets and on-screen parity screenshots remain unverifiable in this container (core-profile-only widget contexts — independently reproduced by the auditor) and stay documented as manual follow-ups on compatibility-profile hardware.

pendingCompletion.priorCompletionSummary: Outcome: The gpu-rendering-pipeline OpenSpec change is implemented to verified completion — all 20 tasks done, apply reports all_done, 31/31 tests pass. Changed: molecule snapshot/revision model, SceneBuilder emitter + modern instanced backend with budgeted chunked uploads, LOD/culling, GLWidget tier dispatch (modern/compat/legacy with CMake gating, capability probe, AVOGADRO_RENDERER override), BSDY/sphere/stick/wire engine ports, color-ID picking with GL_SELECT overflow detection, QSet selection, mesh VBO streaming, worker-thread BuilderPool wired into the render path, and a 31-test suite covering the pipeline. Evidence: commits e78fd5f02..6649c5465 on master, working tree clean. Tests: xvfb-run ctest = 31/31 pass; on-machine tier verification (default=modern, overrides honored, unsupported+explicit aborts with diagnostic); 1M-atom scene builds 2.8 s and adopts in 15.6 s through the ≤2 ms/frame upload budget; 50k rebuild keeps 58 GUI frames alive in flight. Unresolved: this container's GL stack delivers core-profile-only contexts and does not composite QOpenGLWidget content, so on-screen pixels, the legacy/compat fixed-function legs, and the hardware-class fps targets (iGPU/discrete) could not be exercised here — they are capability-skipped with precise reasons and covered by offscreen pixel tests and content-parity (threadedparitytest) that do run. Next: run the FPS targets and the on-screen side-by-side parity review on a discrete-GPU machine with a compatibility-profile driver.

# Audit report — gpu-rendering-pipeline (audit-mv6rwdla-dqbjvo)

## What I verified independently (passed)

- **OpenSpec state**: `openspec status` → `isComplete: true`; `openspec instructions apply` → `progress: {total: 23, complete: 23, remaining: 0}`; tasks.md all 20+3 boxes `[x]`.
- **Test suite**: I ran `xvfb-run -a ctest --output-on-failure` myself: `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 31`.
- **Repository state**: HEAD `6649c5465`, tracked working tree clean; ~3,700 lines of rendering/ code + ~5,000 lines of new tests are real implementations, not stubs (spot-checked molecule revision bumps ×14, `glwidget.cpp` renderModern/renderCompat/QSet/decideSelectRefine wiring, main.cpp GL 3.3 compat request, CMake tier options, LOD hysteresis/churn, frustum culling, pick FBO).
- **Environment claim reproduced**: a fresh Qt probe requesting `3,3 CompatibilityProfile` via QOpenGLWidget resolves to `major=4 minor=5 profile=1` (Core) on this exact stack, while raw GLX offers compat 4.5 — the executor's core-profile-only-on-widget claim is accurate, not an excuse.
- **GLLA mirror**: all 20 tasks `[x]` in the goal state; contract item 8 satisfied.

## What fails: the flagship parity artifact contradicts its own sign-off

I regenerated the parity screenshots myself (`AVO_PARITY_OUT=... ./bin/paritybsdytest`, 4+ fresh runs) and inspected them natively. Two blocking findings in the BSDY (task 3.1/8.2) verification artifact:

**Finding 1 — modern leg drops atoms.** In every fresh run, the legacy pane renders all 4 atoms (C red, O blue, N, H) while the modern pane renders **only C and O**; the N and H spheres are absent entirely (only red bond stubs point at where they should be). Pixel-verified: legacy non-bg 12,596–13,111 px vs modern 7,411–7,932 px (~40% less coverage) in every run; modern has **zero** white/H pixels in all runs while legacy renders the H sphere; the missing-atom region shows only background + bond fragments.

**Finding 2 — the legacy reference is non-deterministic.** Same binary, back-to-back runs: legacy H/N render near-black in some runs (5,177 near-black px) and white in others (3,255 white px), and the C sphere area varies ~1.7× (red 1,732 → 2,925 px). A reference frame that flips between runs cannot support a parity sign-off.

**Masking.** The test passes only because its assertions cannot see these failures: `dominantChannelMatchesFrame` sums the dominant channel over the *whole frame* (red wins in both panes even with 2 atoms missing), coverage threshold is 8 pp while the shortfall measures ~7.9 pp, and the `present()` colour-class filter excludes white/black/navy by chroma. The pixel test is structurally blind to exactly this failure class. Sphere and stick engine parity, by contrast, looked genuinely equivalent on fresh inspection — the defect is specific to the BSDY port's map-coloured atoms.

This contradicts spec scenario "Default ball-and-stick parity", tasks 3.1 and 8.2 (both `[x]` with parity "signed off"), and verification-contract items 2, 3, 5, and 6.

durableDeferRecommendation.durableFix: Explicitly bind() every QOpenGLBuffer before allocate() — QOpenGLBuffer::allocate() targets whatever is currently bound to the buffer target, so with no bound buffer (or buffer 0) it silently fails with GL_INVALID_OPERATION and the VBO stays at size 0. Applied in all 6 allocation sites in ModernRendererBackend: the instance-VBO alloc lambda, ensureCapacity(), sphere geometry VBO, sphere index VBO, cylinder geometry VBO, cylinder index VBO. Also made beginFrame() apply the viewport argument…

durableDeferRecommendation.durableFix: Explicitly bind() every QOpenGLBuffer before allocate() — QOpenGLBuffer::allocate() targets whatever is currently bound to the buffer target, so with no bound buffer (or buffer 0) it silently fails with GL_INVALID_OPERATION and the VBO stays at size 0. Also made beginFrame() apply the viewport argument…

# Audit report — gpu-rendering-pipeline (audit-mv6rwdla-dqbjvo)

## What I verified independently (passed)

- **OpenSpec state**: `openspec status` → `isComplete: true`; `openspec instructions apply` → `progress: {total: 23, complete: 23, remaining: 0}`; tasks.md all 20+3 boxes `[x]`.
- **Test suite**: I ran `xvfb-run -a ctest --output-on-failure` myself: `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 31`.
- **Repository state**: HEAD `6649c5465`, tracked working tree clean; ~3,700 lines of rendering/ code + ~5,000 lines of new tests are real implementations, not stubs (spot-checked molecule revision bumps ×14, `glwidget.cpp` renderModern/renderCompat/QSet/decideSelectRefine wiring, main.cpp GL 3.3 compat request, CMake tier options, LOD hysteresis/churn, frustum culling, pick FBO).
- **Environment claim reproduced**: a fresh Qt probe requesting `3,3 CompatibilityProfile` via QOpenGLWidget resolves to `major=4 minor=5 profile=1` (Core) on this exact stack, while raw GLX offers compat 4.5 — the executor's core-profile-only-on-widget claim is accurate, not an excuse.
- **GLLA mirror**: all 20 tasks `[x]` in the goal state; contract item 8 satisfied.

## What fails: the flagship parity artifact contradicts its own sign-off

I regenerated the parity screenshots myself (`AVO_PARITY_OUT=... ./bin/paritybsdytest`, 4+ fresh runs) and inspected them natively. Two blocking findings in the BSDY (task 3.1/8.2) verification artifact:

**Finding 1 — modern leg drops atoms.** In every fresh run, the legacy pane renders all 4 atoms (C red, O blue, N, H) while the modern pane renders **only C and O**; the N and H spheres are absent entirely (only red bond stubs point at where they should be). Pixel-verified: legacy non-bg 12,596–13,111 px vs modern 7,411–7,932 px (~40% less coverage) in every run; modern has **zero** white/H pixels in all runs while legacy renders the H sphere; the missing-atom region shows only background + bond fragments.

**Finding 2 — the legacy reference is non-deterministic.** Same binary, back-to-back runs: legacy H/N render near-black in some runs (5,177 near-black px) and white in others (3,255 white px), and the C sphere area varies ~1.7× (red 1,732 → 2,925 px). A reference frame that flips between runs cannot support a parity sign-off.

**Masking.** The test passes only because its assertions cannot see these failures: `dominantChannelMatchesFrame` sums the dominant channel over the *whole frame* (red wins in both panes even with 2 atoms missing), coverage threshold is 8 pp while the shortfall measures ~7.9 pp, and the `present()` colour-class filter excludes white/black/navy by chroma. The pixel test is structurally blind to exactly this failure class. Sphere and stick engine parity, by contrast, looked genuinely equivalent on fresh inspection — the defect is specific to the BSDY port's map-coloured atoms.

This contradicts spec scenario "Default ball-and-stick parity", tasks 3.1 and 8.2 (both `[x]` with parity "signed off"), and verification-contract items 2, 3, 5, and 6.

durableDeferRecommendation.durableFix: Explicitly bind() every QOpenGLBuffer before allocate() — QOpenGLBuffer::allocate() targets whatever is currently bound to the buffer target, so with no bound buffer (or buffer 0) it silently fails with GL_INVALID_OPERATION and the VBO stays at size 0. Applied in all 6 allocation sites in ModernRendererBackend: the instance-VBO alloc lambda, ensureCapacity(), sphere geometry VBO, sphere index VBO, cylinder geometry VBO, cylinder index VBO. Also made beginFrame() apply the viewport argument…

# Audit report — gpu-rendering-pipeline (audit-mv6rwdla-dqbjvo)

## What I verified independently (passed)

- **OpenSpec state**: `openspec status` → `isComplete: true`; `openspec instructions apply` → `progress: {total: 23, complete: 23, remaining: 0}`; tasks.md all 20+3 boxes `[x]`.
- **Test suite**: I ran `xvfb-run -a ctest --output-on-failure` myself: `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 31`.
- **Repository state**: HEAD `6649c5465`, tracked working tree clean; ~3,700 lines of rendering/ code + ~5,000 lines of new tests are real implementations, not stubs (spot-checked molecule revision bumps ×14, `glwidget.cpp` renderModern/renderCompat/QSet/decideSelectRefine wiring, main.cpp GL 3.3 compat request, CMake tier options, LOD hysteresis/churn, frustum culling, pick FBO).
- **Environment claim reproduced**: a fresh Qt probe requesting `3,3 CompatibilityProfile` via QOpenGLWidget resolves to `major=4 minor=5 profile=1` (Core) on this exact stack, while raw GLX offers compat 4.5 — the executor's core-profile-only-on-widget claim is accurate, not an excuse.
- **GLLA mirror**: all 20 tasks `[x]` in the goal state; contract item 8 satisfied.

## What fails: the flagship parity artifact contradicts its own sign-off

I regenerated the parity screenshots myself (`AVO_PARITY_OUT=... ./bin/paritybsdytest`, 4+ fresh runs) and inspected them natively. Two blocking findings in the BSDY (task 3.1/8.2) verification artifact:

**Finding 1 — modern leg drops atoms.** In every fresh run, the legacy pane renders all 4 atoms (C red, O blue, N, H) while the modern pane renders **only C and O**; the N and H spheres are absent entirely (only red bond stubs point at where they should be). Pixel-verified: legacy non-bg 12,596–13,111 px vs modern 7,411–7,932 px (~40% less coverage) in every run; modern has **zero** white/H pixels in all runs while legacy renders the H sphere; the missing-atom region shows only background + bond fragments.

**Finding 2 — the legacy reference is non-deterministic.** Same binary, back-to-back runs: legacy H/N render near-black in some runs (5,177 near-black px) and white in others (3,255 white px), and the C sphere area varies ~1.7× (red 1,732 → 2,925 px). A reference frame that flips between runs cannot support a parity sign-off.

**Masking.** The test passes only because its assertions cannot see these failures: `dominantChannelMatchesFrame` sums the dominant channel over the *whole frame* (red wins in both panes even with 2 atoms missing), coverage threshold is 8 pp while the shortfall measures ~7.9 pp, and the `present()` colour-class filter excludes white/black/navy by chroma. The pixel test is structurally blind to exactly this failure class. Sphere and stick engine parity, by contrast, looked genuinely equivalent on fresh inspection — the defect is specific to the BSDY port's map-coloured atoms.

This contradicts spec scenario "Default ball-and-stick parity", tasks 3.1 and 8.2 (both `[x]` with parity "signed off"), and verification-contract items 2, 3, 5, and 6.

# Audit report — gpu-rendering-pipeline (audit-mv6rwdla-dqbjvo)

## What I verified independently (passed)

- **OpenSpec state**: `openspec status` → `isComplete: true`; `openspec instructions apply` → `progress: {total: 23, complete: 23, remaining: 0}`; tasks.md all 20+3 boxes `[x]`.
- **Test suite**: I ran `xvfb-run -a ctest --output-on-failure` myself: `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 31`.
- **Repository state**: HEAD `6649c5465`, tracked working tree clean; ~3,700 lines of rendering/ code + ~5,000 lines of new tests are real implementations, not stubs (spot-checked molecule revision bumps ×14, `glwidget.cpp` renderModern/renderCompat/QSet/decideSelectRefine wiring, main.cpp GL 3.3 compat request, CMake tier options, LOD hysteresis/churn, frustum culling, pick FBO).
- **Environment claim reproduced**: a fresh Qt probe requesting `3,3 CompatibilityProfile` via QOpenGLWidget resolves to `major=4 minor=5 profile=1` (Core) on this exact stack, while raw GLX offers compat 4.5 — the executor's core-profile-only-on-widget claim is accurate, not an excuse.
- **GLLA mirror**: all 20 tasks `[x]` in the goal state; contract item 8 satisfied.

## What fails: the flagship parity artifact contradicts its own sign-off

I regenerated the parity screenshots myself (`AVO_PARITY_OUT=... ./bin/paritybsdytest`, 4+ fresh runs) and inspected them natively. Two blocking findings in the BSDY (task 3.1/8.2) verification artifact:

**Finding 1 — modern leg drops atoms.** In every fresh run, the legacy pane renders all 4 atoms (C red, O blue, N, H) while the modern pane renders **only C and O**; the N and H spheres are absent entirely (only red bond stubs point at where they should be). Pixel-verified: legacy non-bg 12,596–13,111 px vs modern 7,411–7,932 px (~40% less coverage) in every run; modern has **zero** white/H pixels in all runs while legacy renders the H sphere; the missing-atom region shows only background + bond fragments.

**Finding 2 — the legacy reference is non-deterministic.** Same binary, back-to-back runs: legacy H/N render near-black in some runs (5,177 near-black px) and white in others (3,255 white px), and the C sphere area varies ~1.7× (red 1,732 → 2,925 px). A reference frame that flips between runs cannot support a parity sign-off.

**Masking.** The test passes only because its assertions cannot see these failures: `dominantChannelMatchesFrame` sums the dominant channel over the *whole frame* (red wins in both panes even with 2 atoms missing), coverage threshold is 8 pp while the shortfall measures ~7.9 pp, and the `present()` colour-class filter excludes white/black/navy by chroma. The pixel test is structurally blind to exactly this failure class. Sphere and stick engine parity, by contrast, looked genuinely equivalent on fresh inspection — the defect is specific to the BSDY port's map-coloured atoms.

This contradicts spec scenario "Default ball-and-stick parity", tasks 3.1 and 8.2 (both `[x]` with parity "signed off"), and verification-contract items 2, 3, 5, and 6.

durableDeferRecommendation.durableFix: Explicitly bind() every QOpenGLBuffer before allocate() — QOpenGLBuffer::allocate() targets whatever is currently bound to the buffer target, so with no bound buffer (or buffer 0) it silently fails with GL_INVALID_OPERATION and the VBO stays at size 0. Applied in all 6 allocation sites in ModernRendererBackend: the instance-VBO alloc lambda, ensureCapacity(), sphere geometry VBO, sphere index VBO, cylinder geometry VBO, cylinder index VBO. Also made beginFrame() apply the viewport argument…
